quality: The look is a warm burl finish on a clean, flat-front case. Beveled door edges act as hidden pulls, the two doors open onto two adjustable shelves (15 lb each), and cord cutouts in the back let it double as a media console for TVs up to 65".

Construction is engineered wood with rubberwood parts, flat-packed for home assembly, with a 90-day warranty. Expect typical big-box quality for the price; solid wood or real burl veneer costs considerably more.

maker.name: Crosley
paragraphs: Crosley is best known for retro record players and radios. The furniture line launched in 2009 out of Louisville, Kentucky, and now sells through big-box and online retailers including Target, Walmart, Kohl's, Overstock and Urban Outfitters. Products are developed by an internal team rather than credited designers.

The name traces to Powel Crosley's Cincinnati radio company of the 1920s. Today two separate companies sell under the Crosley name: Crosley Brands in Louisville (record players and this furniture) and the Crosley Corporation in North Carolina.
